clue.text: Sullen Ed bashed, beaten for such obstinacy

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a sulky man called Ed as punishment for his stubbornness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bashed' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'beaten' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinacy is stubborn refusal to give way, the same as being pig-headed or mulish.

clue.text: Tops of unripe mangoes and melons I used to create something savoury

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so the first letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: A cook makes a savoury dish from unripe fruit and a personal touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the fifth basic taste, the meaty savoury flavour found in broths and soy sauce.

clue.text: Almost running behind time, through this country

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: running behind time means late
via means through, by way of

explanation.surface: A traveller, nearly late, passes through a country on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic state, a country between Estonia and Lithuania.

clue.text: A way to get to the continent: une route involved with NL?

definitions.text: A way to get to the continent

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: French 'une route' plus the Netherlands code suggests a road to mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'une route' is French for 'a road', which suits the surface, but its letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Tunnel rail link carries travellers from Britain to mainland Europe.

clue.text: Really enjoys archaeological works

definitions.meaning: slang: someone who ... something likes it a lot
excavation sites where archaeologists work are called ...

explanation.surface: An enthusiast loves excavation projects.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb and noun for excavating: slang liking and excavation sites.

clue.text: Looking for water? Get a boat, then give us a sea shanty, perhaps …

parts.note: a dow is a variant spelling of dhow, an Arab sailing boat

parts.words: give us a sea shanty, perhaps
parts.note: to give us a sea shanty is to sing, a sea shanty being one example of a song

explanation.surface: A sailor hires a boat and is asked to sing a sea shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which carries on the singing theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Water divining with a forked rod is a search for underground water sources.

clue.text: .. indeed, other ditties and prayers

parts.note: even can mean indeed, as in 'it was good, even excellent'
ditties are songs; 'other' links back to the sea shanty of the previous clue

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the singer adds more ditties and prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening church services of the Anglican liturgy, sung prayers at day's end.

clue.text: Blended ale in grand vats to get a wonderful crisp taste

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: Beer mixed in big vats yields a fine, sharp flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crisp' looks like describing the taste, but it means a potato crisp, the British word for a chip in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite British potato crisp flavour, the classic chip-shop seasoning.

clue.text: Those who draw attention to foul play: referees, perhaps?

definitions.text: Those who draw attention to foul play
definitions.meaning: people who expose wrongdoing in an organisation
referees literally blow a whistle, a cryptic example

explanation.surface: People who expose cheating are compared to match officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Informants exposing misconduct, and also match officials signalling a foul by whistle.

clue.text: Catch ruffian grabbing muzzle of revolver: it's placed nearby to fire

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a thug is a violent ruffian

indicators.note: the muzzle is the front end of a gun, so the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Arresting a gunman who holds a revolver, ready to fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' suggests shooting, but it means a domestic fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rug laid in front of a fireplace to protect the floor from sparks.

clue.text: Wide part of foot in instrument of torture

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
the heel is the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: A wide part of the foot is caught in a torture device.
explanation.definitionFit: Victims were once broken on a large spoked wheel, a medieval torture device.

clue.text: This could start you off on the slippery slope

definitions.text: This could start you off on the slippery slope

parts.words: This could start you off on the slippery slope
parts.note: 'slippery slope' usually means a path to ruin, but here it is a snowy run that skiers are carried up to

explanation.surface: A warning about the first step toward moral decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical tow carries skiers uphill to the top of a snowy run.

clue.text: Ms Farrow's mother creating an unwholesome atmosphere?

parts.note: the actress Mia Farrow, so the possessive gives MIA'S
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mia Farrow's mother made the air unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour or oppressive, unhealthy air.

clue.text: Diplomat — American with business degrees — getting unhappy with men

parts.note: MBA is a Master of Business Administration, plural MBAS
sad means unhappy
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An American envoy with business qualifications is depressed by his staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-ranking envoy representing one state in another is a senior diplomat.

clue.text: Hole in the wall? Collect stake money on the way back

indicators.note: going back means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to pool money is to collect stakes together into one fund

explanation.surface: Using a cash machine to gather betting money on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole in the wall' suggests a cash machine, but here it is a slit in a castle wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a loophole, a narrow opening in a fortified wall for shooting through.

clue.text: Drink providing sustenance to Ulstermen, you might say?

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, so the spelling heard is swapped for one that sounds the same

parts.note: Orangemen are Ulster Protestants, so help for them is orange aid

explanation.surface: A beverage offered as help to Northern Irish loyalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternity strong in Northern Ireland (Ulster).
explanation.definitionFit: A soft drink flavoured with citrus fruit, a fizzy fruit beverage.

clue.text: I'm nude, with a gin, dancing: that's unforeseen

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party guest boasts of dancing naked, drink in hand: nobody expected it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never pictured beforehand was unexpected and not anticipated.

clue.text: Lad fighting with barkeep: could this make him stop?

indicators.note: fighting means scrapping and in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A young man brawls with a barman: what might halt him?
explanation.definitionFit: The foot control in a car that slows or halts the vehicle.

clue.text: Len — meet troubled Al, maybe

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Len is told to meet a friend called Al, who is having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: Al looks like a man's name but is the chemical symbol for aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium, symbol Al, is one example of a chemical substance in the periodic table.

clue.text: Wine could get adult moving — sit!

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: moving letters change place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drink might set a grown-up dancing, so they are told to sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white from Piedmont.

clue.text: Health check from crank returning to take English at university

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a crank or eccentric
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: An eccentric comes back to study English and gets a medical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Health check' here is a service for an engine, as well as a fitness check.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine service or adjustment that keeps an engine, or a body, in good working order.

clue.text: Cor! Giesela holds such wild parties!

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the answer is concealed within the words

explanation.surface: An admiring exclamation about a woman who hosts riotous parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Debauched revels, gatherings of unrestrained excess.

clue.text: Beard not properly shaven: could it be the last straw?

definitions.meaning: short bristly growth on an unshaven face

definitions.text: could it be the last straw?
definitions.meaning: the stalks of cereal left in a field after harvest, the straw remaining at the end

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a scruffy unshaven chin is finally too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bristle on a chin and the cut stalks left after reaping.

clue.text: Coffin-bearer embracing king and gang member?

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bier is the stand on which a coffin is carried
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A pallbearer hugging a monarch is perhaps a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist, perhaps a member of a motorbike gang like the Hells Angels.

clue.text: Pine part of guitar

definitions.meaning: to pine is to worry or grieve
a raised ridge across the fingerboard of a guitar

explanation.surface: Pine wood used for a guitar section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' suggests the wood a guitar is built from, but it is a verb: to worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to worry anxiously and also a ridge on a guitar's fingerboard.

clue.text: Blank out periods of time with ecstasy

parts.note: eras are long periods of time
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Whole stretches of memory are lost through taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To blank something out is to wipe or delete it completely.

clue.text: Black-eyed Susan crashed a red Buick

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman with a bruised eye smashed her red car.
explanation.walkthrough: Black-eyed Susan sounds like an injured driver; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like North American flower with yellow petals and a dark centre, called Black-eyed Susan.

clue.text: Just you watch it … don't be a part of their game

definitions.text: Just you watch it … don't be a part of their game

parts.words: Just you watch it … don't be a part of their game
parts.note: reads as a threat, but describes a game people watch rather than play

explanation.surface: A menacing warning to keep out of someone's schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport whose appeal lies in being watched by crowds rather than played by them.
